entries.answer: The launcher is the control layer for the GTA V iOS project. It handles project-specific setup, graphics options, controls, mod import, and other runtime choices before the game starts.

If the launcher itself will not open, first confirm the app is still validly signed, that iOS can launch the app normally, and that you have enough free storage. If it closes immediately, capture the crash report or launcher log instead of repeatedly reinstalling.
Reset launcher settings only when you want to remove a bad configuration. Before resetting, note any custom graphics, controls, mod, or path choices so you can restore them one by one.
Use the current project update instructions rather than replacing files blindly. Back up saves first, then follow the release-specific install or re-sign steps for the build you are moving to.
Use the selected app build in Franklin's session setup or attach run.log so the build can be matched against the project release list. Do not guess the build from the installation date alone.
Use the project's current release path and Discord instructions for the active build. Avoid mirrors or reuploaded IPAs because they can be outdated, modified, or signed differently.

An IPA installation failure is usually separate from an in-game crash. Check the signing method, certificate or provisioning status, available storage, and whether the IPA was modified after signing. Keep the exact installer error because it narrows the cause.

If the signing profile expires or is revoked, iOS may refuse to launch the app even though the game files are intact. Re-sign using your supported sideloading method and protect your saves before replacing the installation.

If iOS reports an untrusted developer, finish the trust or developer-mode steps required by your signing method. The exact menu can differ by iOS version and signing tool, so follow that tool's current instructions.

Some sideloading methods require iOS Developer Mode. If your installer explicitly requires it, enable it through the iOS privacy and security settings, restart if requested, and then try launching the signed app again.
Use the folder structure documented by the current project guide. Do not rename archives or move only part of the game data unless the guide for your build says to do so.

Missing or incomplete game data can cause startup failure, endless loading, or archive errors. Compare the installed folder structure with the guide and replace only the missing or damaged data from your own legitimate game copy.

The compatibility policy treats 20 GB or less free space as insufficient working headroom, 21 to 30 GB as limited, and more than 30 GB as preferred. Extraction, updates, caches, and logs all need temporary space.

If a file picker or import flow cannot see the expected file, check whether the file is actually stored locally or in an accessible Files location. Cloud-only placeholders may need to download before the launcher can import them.
Nearby discovery on iPhone or iPad depends on Local Network access. If the permission was denied, enable it for the app in iOS settings and retry while both devices are on the same Wi-Fi.

The host creates a GTA Online session and shares its session code. A friend opens Join, chooses ENTER CODE, and enters that code. Connection can still fail if the network blocks direct peer-to-peer traffic.

For an invalid or failed session code, first confirm both players are on compatible project builds and that the code was copied exactly. If the code is accepted but connection fails, test Wi-Fi and router conditions next.

UPnP can help a host router create mappings for peer-to-peer sessions. Only change router settings if you understand the network and have permission to do so. A mobile carrier or restrictive network can still block direct connections.

Some mobile networks use NAT or filtering that makes direct peer-to-peer connections unreliable. If a session fails on cellular data, test a normal Wi-Fi network before assuming the launcher or game is broken.

Story Mode itself does not need a multiplayer session. Whether the app needs connectivity for signing, downloads, or a project feature depends on your installation method and build, so separate launch requirements from actual Story Mode gameplay.
The launcher can support project-compatible mods, but compatibility depends on the file type and what the mod changes. Back up affected files before importing and test one mod at a time.

Use only mod formats the launcher explicitly supports for your build. OIV and RPF-based content are part of the current mod workflow discussed in this project; do not assume ScriptHook-based packages will work on the native iOS port.

Do not assume ScriptHook or Windows ASI plugins work on this native iOS port. Mods that depend on PC injection, ScriptHook, or platform-specific DLL behavior need a compatible implementation rather than simple file copying.

When a mod import fails, keep the full error message and identify the package type. A bad archive structure, unsupported installer instruction, conflicting target path, or damaged package can all look like a generic import failure.
If the game broke after adding mods, disable or restore the most recent mod first. Add mods back one at a time so you can identify the first package that changes the behavior.
A language pack can fail if it targets a different game archive or build layout. Verify the pack matches the project version, then restore the original language files before trying another pack.
Back up your save data before re-signing, reinstalling, replacing game data, or testing major mods. Treat a backup as required whenever an operation may replace the app container.
A reinstall can replace the app container depending on the signing and installation method. Do not assume saves survive. Back them up before removing the current app.

If a save no longer loads, test whether a new save works first. If new saves work, the old save may be incompatible or damaged; if no saves work, check the game data and current build before blaming the save file.

Do not overwrite your only copy of a suspected corrupt save. Duplicate it first, test another known-good save, and keep the original while you narrow down whether the problem is the save or the current game build.

The project maps touch controls through a virtual XInput-style layer and also supports physical controller use in the documented control path. If a controller connects to iOS but the game ignores it, test input without custom mappings first.

Confirm the controller works in iOS before troubleshooting the game. Then reconnect it, remove custom remaps, and launch with the default control profile. If touch works but the controller does not, report the controller model and build.

If touch controls stop responding, check whether a physical controller is connected and whether the touch overlay was hidden. Then restore the default HUD/control layout and retry before reinstalling.
